## Claims
- [source-backed] A bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\in S_n\) is indexed by \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\); \(J_v=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{\sigma_u:u\ge v\}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 67-78]
- [source-backed] The coefficient ring is the integral symmetric-function ring \(\Lambda=\Lambda(x_1,x_2,\ldots)\); \(I_{r,n-r}=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{s_\lambda:\lambda\nsubseteq(n-r)^r\}\), and \(H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong\overline\Lambda:=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 89-94]
- [source-backed] Theorem 1.2 sets \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), and concludes that \(J_v\), as an ideal of \(\overline\Lambda\), is minimally generated by \(\{\overline{s}_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\). Here minimality means that no generator can be removed. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 95-110]
- [source-backed] The proof mechanism uses integral Schur-basis multiplication and the quotient rule \(\overline s_\lambda\overline s_\mu=\sum_{\nu\subseteq(n-r)^r}c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\nu}\overline s_\nu\). A hypothetical removable generator produces a syzygy among the displayed generators; homogeneity reduces it to a system of integral linear equations. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 136-160]
- [source-backed] The proof establishes inconsistency of the resulting decomposable linear system whenever wide equations have right side \(0\) and some tall equation has nonzero right side; consequently no such syzygy exists. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 473-501]
- [source-backed] Corollary 4.6 records the resulting irredundance: for every bigrassmannian \(v\) with the Theorem 1.2 parameters, \(\{\overline{s}_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) minimally generates \(J_v\) in \(\overline\Lambda\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 503-506]
- [source-backed] The proof text separately notes that \(i=n-r\) implies \(a=0\), making Theorem 1.2 trivial; the supplied conversion corrupts the following displayed proof-only parameter restrictions, so no further exact restrictions are extracted here. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 143-149]
- [source-backed] The source’s Remark 4.7 says the transposed family \(\{\overline{s}_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) would require transposing the arguments; this proof passage does not itself assert that family’s minimality. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 507-512]

## Strategy
Extracted the theorem’s integral presentation, its full stated bigrassmannian and parameter hypotheses, and the proof chain: hypothetical syzygy \(\Rightarrow\) integral linear system \(\Rightarrow\) inconsistency \(\Rightarrow\) no removable generator.

## Gaps
The retrieved HTML corrupts part of the proof-only “valid tuple” display near lines 147–164. The exact proof-only inequalities beyond the theorem’s stated hypotheses are therefore unresolved.
